title: Establishing standard values for upper body posture in relation to postural control in older people
summary:
This is a one-time measurement. The study will include 253 male and female participants.
 For measurement with the three-dimensional back scanner, the test person stands barefoot with their back uncovered approximately 90 cm in front of the device. The back of the test person is optically captured and recorded using a light strip grid. The scanner first records six marked fixed points on the back and reproduces these in a phase image, a depth image and a two-dimensional image. The upper body posture is recorded by projecting a light strip pattern onto the back, which is captured by an integrated LCD camera in the scanner and converted into a phase image by the software. Each measurement takes approximately 1 minute. 
To measure postural control with the pressure measurement plate, the test person stands barefoot on a pressure measurement plate from GeBioM. Postural control is thus determined and recorded over a measurement period of 3 times 30 seconds.

Each measurement with both the back scanner and the pressure measurement plate is performed three times.

interventions.name:
The aim of the study is to generate standard values for upper body posture and postural control in men and women aged 65 and over who subjectively feel healthy, within the framework of a cross-sectional analysis.
The study comprises a single measurement on 253 male and female test subjects.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-No health problems according to subjective assessment
-No operations or acute complaints or injuries to the musculoskeletal system within the last 2 years.
Exclusion criteria:
- Complaints, pain, disorders of the spine, shoulders and pelvis
- Operations/injuries in the area of the spine, shoulders or pelvis
- Current physiotherapy or orthopaedic therapy
- Use of muscle relaxants
- Complaints in the musculoskeletal system
- Medically diagnosed physical malpositions
